REPORT

S. 1, Special Branch, XXXXXX File No.................... Date October 27, 1941.

SUBJECT: Strike of Carpenters and Masons -
settlement and proposed meeting of
building contractors on October 30,
1941.

Through direct negotiations between representatives
of employers and those of employees, the strike of
approximately 3,000 casual carpenters and masons, which
was declared on October 16 to enforce a demand for
100% increase in wages, was settled on October 25 and
the workers resumed on October 26.

Both parties have agreed upon the following
increases in wages to be effective from November 15:-

| Classification of workers | New wages per day | Existing wages per day |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Carpenters | $3.30 | $2.00 |
| Masons | $3.10 | $1.90 |
| Apprentices (Carpenters) | $1.20 | $0.75 |
| Apprentices (Masons) | $1.10 | $0.70 |

These workers are supplied with food by the employers.

At 3 p.m., October 30, some 50 building
contractors will hold a meeting on the premises of the
Tsung Nyi Society, 7th floor, Sz Soh Building, Nanking
Road, to enable the representatives to report on the
terms of settlement. Messrs. Kiang Zang Kung
(江長庚), Zia Ping Hung (謝秉衡) and Chang
Chi Kwang (張继光), representatives of the
employers, called at Special Branch at 3.35 p.m.,
October 27 and requested permission for the holding
of the proposed meeting.

On October 17, a joint despatch was received at Special Branch Headquarters from the Shanghai Municipality 1st, 2nd, 3rd, and 6th District Masons & Carpenters Unions (with offices at Room 401, House 210 Kiukiang Road), requesting the Police to place on record the present strike declared by a portion of masons and carpenters on October 16 to enforce a demand for a 100% increase in wages.

As no agreement was reached during the meeting held on October 21, between representatives of the employers and employees, for negotiating a settlement in the strike, a suggestion was put forward at the meeting that representatives of both the labour and capital attend Special Branch Police Headquarters for mediation but this was rejected by the labour representatives.

As will be seen from the above facts the four unions are incorporated into one organization, who would be influenced by the Shanghai Special Municipality Social Movement Direction Committee which is the chief supporter of the Committee, rather than by the Municipal Police.

It is also to be noted that the masons and carpenters are of low mentality and have not the initiative to be active in the union affairs. It is confidentially learned that the union is entirely in the hands of the clerk who is a follower of Hu Shou-chi (胡寿祺), a professional agitator, who is also at present a committee member of the Social Movement Direction Committee and concurrently Chairman of the "Chinese Ratepayers' Association" of the Nanking

Translation of a joint dispatch dated October 17, 1941
addressed to Special Branch, S.M.P., by the "Shanghai
Municipality First, Second, Third and Sixth District
Masons and Carpenters Unions".

To the Special Branch,
S. M. P.

Sirs,

Sometime ago we received a letter from Ghui Kwang
Hwa (瞿光華) and other members of the Joint
Representative Group of local Masons and Carpenters,
stating that owing to the continuous rising cost of
living, they are unable to make ~~their~~ ends meet
with their present earnings and they requested us to
approach the Building Contractors Association to increase
their wages. After several discussions, the Building
Contractors Association agreed to call a meeting of
representatives of the labour and capital at 3 p.m.
October 21 to hold a discussion on the issue. Ghui
Kwang Hwa and other representatives of the masons and
carpenters were accordingly informed by letter to attend
the meeting at the appointed time and date.

However, the workers, holding the view that the
date of the meeting was far too remote and that the
employers showed lack of sincerity in the negotiations,
declared a "taiekung" strike on the morning of October 16
and by 4 p.m. the same day, they struck work completely.
Although our Unions have detailed officials to advise
the workers to resume work and not to resort to lawless
activities pending a solution of the dispute at the
meeting to be held on October 21, our efforts have ended
in failure due to the leaders' obstinacy. Fearing
a possible aggravation of the situation, we have,
therefore, sent this communication requesting that your
Branch will place the matter on record.

Reference the report submitted on October 16

informed of the date of the proposed general meeting,
immediately accused the employers of having wilfully
ignored the time-limit, which the workers claim should
be on October 19 instead of October 21 as scheduled.
As a protest they commenced a strike on October 16.

The portion of carpenters and masons at present
affected, consisting chiefly of casual workers and
numbering some 3,000 covering the three areas, are
still on strike to-day, October 17. The present wages
being $4.40 per diem, they are now demanding an
increase of 100%.

Despite the obstinate and threatening attitude
of the carpenters and masons who commenced the strike
on October 16 and with the assistance of certain
professional agitators, it is understood that
the employers have decided not to yield to their demands.

To Special Branch, S.M.P.

These unions came into existence in 1927. In
the same year, with the approval of official organs and
in the presence of their representatives, we signed an
agreement with the Building Contractors Association.
It was agreed that we could function within the Internation-
al Settlement and French Concession.

As a result of cooperation between capital and
labour, no strikes were declared by the workers in the
trade during the past fourteen years and all disputes
were settled amicably through our mediation. Recently
the workers demanded an increase in wages owing to the
high cost of living and the employers, at our request,
convened a meeting on March 26 with the permission of the
Settlement Authorities for the purpose of discussing the
matter. It was decided that carpenters, who are receiving
$1.00 per day, be granted an increase of 90 cents per day,
making a total of $1.90; that masons, who are receiving
95 cents per day, be granted an increase of 80 cents per
day, making a total of $1.75 per day; and that apprentices
be granted an increase of 25 cents per day. All the
workers are given food. In other words, the workers
were granted 90% - 100% increase in wages. This decision
was published in the press by the employers for the
information of those concerned.

致工部局警务处特务科。

本工会成立于1927年。同年，在官方机构批准及其代表在场的情况下，我们与建筑承包商协会签署了一项协议。协议约定我们可以在国际租界和法租界内开展活动。

由于劳资合作，过去十四年间，本行业工人未宣布过任何罢工，所有纠纷均通过我们的调解友好解决。最近，由于生活成本高企，工人要求增加工资，应我方请求，雇主在租界当局的许可下，于3月26日召开会议讨论此事。会议决定，目前日薪为$1.00的木匠，每日加薪90分，总计$1.90；目前日薪为95分的泥瓦匠，每日加薪80分，总计每日$1.75；学徒每日加薪25分。所有工人均提供膳食。换言之，工人获得了90% - 100%的工资增长。雇主已将此决定刊登于报刊，以便相关人员知悉。

page_data.en:
- 2 -

Unexpectedly a portion of the workers, at the
instigation of outsiders, have organized a "Masons and
Carpenters Welfare Society" in the Settlement for the
purpose of agitation. They compelled the workers to
declare a strike under the pretext that the recent
increase would be insufficient to meet the growing
cost of living, thereby endangering the peace and good
order of the Settlement. Our efforts to stop the
strike were of no avail as the workers had been deprived
of their tools by the agitators.

Our unions are legitimate and cooperating
with the employers. Following the return of the
"National Government" to Nanking, we affected registration
with the Shanghai Branch of the Social Movement Direction
Committee. In order to avoid misunderstanding in
connection with the present strike, which was caused by
certain agitators, we have applied to the Shanghai Branch,
Social Movement Direction Committee, for investigation.
In addition, we hereby apply to you for assistance **〔此处转录不清〕** in order to maintain peace and good order
and to facilitate our labour movement.

(chopped) Shanghai 1st District
Masons and Carpenters Union.

(chopped) Shanghai 6th District
Masons and Carpenters Union.

- 2 -

出乎意料的是，一部分工人在外人煽动下，在租界组织了一个“泥瓦匠与木匠福利社”，旨在进行煽动。他们以近期加薪不足以应对日益增长的生活成本为借口，强迫工人宣布罢工，从而危及租界的和平与良好秩序。我们阻止罢工的努力未能奏效，因为工人的工具已被煽动者夺走。

我们的工会是合法的，并与雇主合作。随着“国民政府”还都南京，我们在社会运动指导委员会上海分会进行了注册。为了避免因某些煽动者引起的当前罢工产生误解，我们已向社会运动指导委员会上海分会申请调查。此外，我们特此向贵处申请协助 **〔此处转录不清〕** ，以维持和平与良好秩序，并促进我们的劳工运动。

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS.

OCT 1 1 1939

AN APPEAL TO OWNERS AND FELLOW
CONTRACTORS
from
THE SHANGHAI BUILDING CONTRACTORS' GUILD

NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that a letter has been received by this
Guild from some of our members, stating as follows:—
"On account of the rapid decline of foreign exchange and high
increase in costs, we have suffered very heavy losses and have
asked in our previous letter for your assistance. We wish to thank
you in this connection for your advertisement in the newspapers
appealing to the owners. Since then we have been communicating
with them for a compromise. Some have made reasonable increases,
some only expressed their sympathy without taking any action,
and others simply escaped from giving clear expression. As we
cannot carry on with further delay, we shall be inevitably compel-
led to suspend our work and wait for a reasonable settlement.
In view of other complications which might arise from the owners'
tendering the incomplete jobs to new contractors after our suspen-
sion, we request that you would advertise in the newspapers to the
effect that all jobs suspended owing to the present situation shall
not be taken up by other persons without first obtaining consent
of the original contractors."
Under the present circumstances, our member contractors have really
encountered serious difficulties, which have set a big obstacle to the
completion of their work and they have no way out of these difficulties
unless some amicable compromise be made. We have previously published
in the newspapers an appeal which we trust has received the attention
of the owners.
We are in deep sympathy with our member contractors as regards
what they have enumerated in their letter. But we would advise them
not to suspend their work before careful consideration is made as, once
the work is suspended, it will be more difficult to reach a settlement and
additional disputes may arise thus making the situation more complicated.
As to the incomplete jobs to be taken up by new contractors, less
anxiety should be felt in consideration of our strong union and the
majority of members who have high business morals and will no doubt
refrain from profiting for themselves at other people's expense.
Since the agreements for construction work are mostly specified with
a time of completion, and the owners would expect to have use of their
property in due time, suspension of jobs will cause unnecessary losses.
Even if the owners should give the incomplete jobs to their new con-
tractors there is no possibility of coming to terms without an increase in
price. Instead of delaying the jobs and losing valuable time, it will be
much better to effect an early completion of work at a reasonable
increase in cost. We believe this point will be thoroughly appreciated by
the owners.
For the interests of both the contractors and the owners we have
herein-above reiterated what we are aware of and hope that our appeal
will be kindly accepted.

1939年10月11日

致业主及同业承包商的呼吁
来自
上海建筑承包商公会

特此通知，本公会收到部分会员来信，内容如下：“由于外汇迅速贬值及成本大幅上涨，我们遭受了严重损失，并在之前的信中请求各位协助。在此方面，我们要感谢各位在报纸上刊登广告向业主发出呼吁。此后，我们一直与他们沟通以寻求妥协。有些业主给予了合理的加价，有些仅表示同情而未采取任何行动，还有些则回避给出明确表态。由于我们无法继续拖延，我们将不可避免地被迫停工，等待合理的解决方案。鉴于若我们在停工后业主将未完工项目转包给新承包商可能会引发其他复杂情况，我们请求各位在报纸上刊登广告，声明所有因当前局势而停工的项目，在未获得原承包商同意的情况下，不得由其他人承接。”
在目前的情况下，我们的会员承包商确实遇到了严重困难，这给完成工作带来了巨大障碍，除非达成某种友好妥协，否则他们无法摆脱这些困难。我们此前已在报纸上发表了一份呼吁，相信已引起业主的关注。
对于会员们在信中列举的情况，我们深表同情。但我们建议他们在仔细考虑之前不要停工，因为一旦停工，达成和解将更加困难，并可能引发额外的纠纷，从而使局势更加复杂。至于未完工项目被新承包商承接的问题，考虑到我们强大的公会以及大多数具有高尚商业道德的会员无疑会 refrain from profiting for themselves at other people's expense（避免损人利己），不必过于担忧。
由于建筑工程合同大多规定了完工时间，业主期望按时使用其房产，停工将造成不必要的损失。即使业主将未完工项目交给新承包商，如果不增加价格，也不可能达成协议。与其拖延工期浪费宝贵时间，不如以合理的成本增加尽早完工。我们相信业主会充分理解这一点。
为了承包商和业主双方的利益，我们在此重申我们所知悉的情况，希望我们的呼吁能得到善意接受。

Central China Daily News :- 4/10/39
WORKMEN OF BUILDING CONTRACTOR CONCERNS SUBMIT
DEMAND FOR AN INCREASE OF WAGES

Owing to the heavy rise in foreign exchange
resulting in a rise in the prices of commodities, some time
ago the workmen of the local building concerns submitted
a demand to the owners for an increase of their wages with
a view to maintaining their livelihood. However, because
of no satisfactory settlement, their demand resulted in a
"go-slow" strike.
Nevertheless the workmen in question fear that
the owners of the properties concerned will engage other
workmen to carry on the jobs by contract after the work has
been suspended by them. Considering that this will
certainly cause some other disputes between the workmen
on strike and those who will be engaged to carry on their
work, the Building Contractors' Guild has therefore advised
all its members not to carry on the uncompleted work in
order not to seize the interests of other members of the
same guild, and hope that the owners in question will grant
the increase so as to prevent the movement from being
further developed.

《华中日报》:- 1939年10月4日
建筑承包商公司的工人提交增加工资的要求

由于外汇大幅上涨导致商品价格上涨，前段时间本地建筑公司的工人为了维持生计，向业主提交了增加工资的要求。然而，由于未能达成令人满意的解决方案，他们的要求导致了“怠工”罢工。
尽管如此，相关工人担心，在他们停工后，相关物业的业主会雇佣其他工人以承包方式继续施工。考虑到这必然会在罢工工人与受雇继续工作的工人之间引发其他纠纷，建筑承包商公会因此建议其所有会员不要继续未完成的工作，以免损害同一公会其他会员的利益，并希望相关业主批准加薪，以防止事态进一步发展。

in view of other complications which might arise from the owners’

in the newspapers an appeal which we trust has received the attenticn 
of the owners.

what they have cnumerated in their letter. But we would advise them 
not to suspend their work before careful consideration is made as, once 
the work is suspended, it will be more difficult ta reach a settlement and 
additional disputes may arise thus making the situation more complicated. 


As to the incomplete jobs to be taken up by new contractors, less 
anxiety should be felt in consideration cf our strong union and the 
majority of members who have high business morals and will na doubt 
refrain from profiting for themselves at other people’s expense. 


Since the agreements for construction work are mostly specified with 
a time of completion, and the owners would expect to haye use of their 
property in due time, suspension of jobs will cause unnecessary losses, 
Even if the owners should give the incomplete jobs to their new con- 
tractors there is no possibility of coming to terms without an increase in 
price... Instead of delaying the jobs and losing valuable time, it will be 
much better to effect an early completion of work at a reasonable 
increase in cast. We believe this point will be thoroughly appreciated by 
the owners. ‘ 


For the interests of both the contractors and the owners we have 
herein-above reiterated what we are aware of and hope that our appeal 
will be kindly accepted.
